title: MUD & IRON
subtitle: Every follower is a soldier. Every day, the front decides.

factions.name: The Hegemony
factions.pitch: Order. Discipline. Iron. Stand with the Empire.

factions.name: The Concord
factions.pitch: Free men in the mud. Stand with the Alliance.

archetypes.name: Rifleman
archetypes.desc: The backbone of the line. Sentry, raids, mud.

archetypes.name: Machine Gunner
archetypes.desc: Holds the line with the gun. Feared by both sides.

archetypes.name: Sapper
archetypes.desc: Digs tunnels under no man's land. Listens to the earth.

archetypes.name: Stretcher Bearer
archetypes.desc: Carries the wounded out. Saves other players' soldiers.

archetypes.name: Runner
archetypes.desc: Carries orders under fire. Knows every trench.

archetypes.name: Sniper
archetypes.desc: Patient, alone, deadly. Duels across the wire.

archetypes.name: Signaller
archetypes.desc: Keeps the wires alive. Hears what others don't.

archetypes.name: Field Cook
archetypes.desc: Feeds the line. Everyone's friend, nobody's target.

archetypes.name: Chaplain
archetypes.desc: Buries the dead, writes the letters, keeps faith.

archetypes.name: Pilot
archetypes.desc: Flies recon over the front. Your side's riflemen shoot better while the plane is up. One per side, chosen by lottery.

milestones.text: A thousand souls in the mud. The generals take notice.
The front grows. New sectors are dug.
Steel monsters arrive from the rear: the first tanks.

dm.enlisted: {rank} @{handle}, you have been assigned to {unit}, sector {sector}. Find yourself on the front: {url}
dm.claim: Your claim code: {code}. Comment it under our latest post to take command of your soldier.

lore.tagline: The Great War ended. Here, it never did.
lore.short: For six winters the Concord and the Hegemony have bled into the same valley of mud. Neither will yield. Both need men. They need you.
lore.concord: The Concord: a ragged alliance of free provinces in khaki and flat steel helmets. They fight for the right to go home. Together, or not at all.
lore.hegemony: The Hegemony: an iron empire in field grey that does not know the word retreat. Order, discipline, the long patience of steel. Iron endures.

@{handle} The Hegemony grows stronger. Report to sector {sector}, soldier 🩶
concord: Welcome to the front, {rank} @{handle}. Your post: sector {sector}. Together, or not at all 🫒 Find yourself via the link in bio.
@{handle} Another hand for the Concord. Report to sector {sector} 🫒

race.reward: Holds the high ground: 3 days of artillery on the enemy, a safer week for its soldiers, a ribbon for everyone on the winning side, and the title of hero for the soldier who tips the balance.

objectives.name: Hill 304
objectives.rewardText: Takes the high ground and its observation tree: for 3 days the winner's snipers and machine gunners shoot straighter, a safer week for its soldiers, a ribbon for everyone on the winning side, and the title of hero for the soldier who tips the balance.

objectives.name: Blackwater Canal
objectives.rewardText: The first side to kill 100 enemy soldiers takes Blackwater Canal: a safer week for its soldiers, a ribbon for everyone on the winning side, and the title of hero for its deadliest soldier.

objectives.name: Grey Mill
objectives._need: 19. 11. (uživatel): 100 nováčků je při stovkách denně hned, zatím 300; nový typ závodu o mlýn čeká na schválení
objectives.rewardText: Takes the mill and a heavy howitzer that stays for good: every day it shells the most crowded stretch of the enemy line. It wears out and can be destroyed; only sappers with time to spare can keep it firing.

objectives.name: the Bone Quarry
objectives.rewardText: Takes the quarry and its tunnels: the winner's sappers dig a mine under the enemy line for one day, and the next day it goes up under the most crowded enemy trench. The crater stays for good. Enemy sappers may hear the digging and cave the tunnel in.

logistics.victory: For {days} days better supplies come up {objective} to the {us} line
logistics._victory: uživatel 19. 11.: hráčům jen „lepší logistika“, ne že střílí víc
logistics._: 19. 11. (uživatel): odměna kóty místo bombardování; vítěz {days} dní střílí {shots}× denně (ostatní 1×).

observation._: odměna kóty s reward 'observation' (Hill 304; místo bombardování, pokyn uživatele 14. 11.): `days` dní od příštího dne mají odstřelovači a kulometčíci vítěze palbu ×(1+fire); web ukáže falešný strom-pozorovatelnu za linií vítěze; noviny každé ráno hlášení
observation.victory: For {days} days the spotters in the observation tree on {objective} will watch every move in the {them} trenches, and the {us} snipers and machine gunners will shoot straighter for it
observation.text: From the observation tree on {objective} the {us} spotters watched the {them} line all day and called out every head that showed. {us} snipers and machine gunners hit {hits} men. {left}
left: The tree keeps watching for {n} more days.
The tree keeps watching for one more day.
Tonight the spotters climb down for the last time.
observation._kill: 15. 11. (uživatel: pozorovatelna musí být znát na smrtích): střelci strany s pozorovatelnou (sniper, MG, puškař) mají palbu ×(1+fire) a šanci zabít na místě ×(1+kill).

race._need: need: výchozí cíl závodu; objectives[].type 'kills' = vyhrává, kdo první zabije `need` nepřátel (padlí soupeře od začátku závodu); Blackwater Canal: kills 100 (uživatel 14. 11.: místo nových vojáků rozhodují zabití)

gun.name: the {objective} gun
gun.victory: The {us} dragged a heavy howitzer into a gun pit behind their line. From tomorrow it fires every day on the most crowded {them} trenches, until it is destroyed. Sappers keep it in repair.
gun._: 20. 11. (uživatel): odměna Grey Mill = jedno těžké dělo natrvalo s opotřebením (engine/gun.js, theme.battle.gun)

mine.victory: From the quarry, {us} sappers started a tunnel under the {them} line. They will dig for a day. The day after, the mine goes up.
mine.text: At dawn the ground under the {them} trench lifted and fell back. The {us} sappers had dug from {name} all night, and the mine went up under sectors {from} to {to}. {hit} {them} men were caught in it, {killed} of them killed outright. The crater will stay. Tunnellers: {diggers}.
mine.collapsed: The {us} sappers were digging a tunnel from {name} under the {them} line. {listeners} {them} sappers took turns listening at the wall of their own trench. They heard the picks, blew a small charge, and the tunnel caved in. The {us} diggers ({diggers}) got out alive. The mine never went off.
mine._: 21. 11. (uživatel): odměna Bone Quarry = mina, kopou jeden den (engine/mine.js, theme.battle.mine)
mine.digging: All day and all night the {us} sappers dug from {name} toward the {them} trench, passing sacks of clay back by hand and keeping the candles low. The tunnel is almost under them. Tomorrow the charge goes in. Diggers: {diggers}.

schedule._note: Denní rytmus v UTC (pevně, bez letního času). editionUtc = nový den války: denní tah, nové číslo novin, vyhodnocení hlasování. reelUtc = večerní reel/příspěvek (fronta marketing/queue.json).

valley._enabled: Výpravy (CHURCH…) jsou vypnuté, dokud je uživatel nezapne; hlasuje se jen o stavbách na IG.
valley._words: Dokud jsou výpravy vypnuté, příběhy s těmito slovy se nepoužijí (stejně jako gunsWords u děl).
valley._note: Výpravy (docs/MAP_MISSIONS.md). Každé `every` dny ranní noviny vyhlásí výpravu, přihlášky do dalšího vydání, `slots` míst na frakci. Místo: x,y v mřížce mapy 192×120, img v web/public/assets/locations (size = velikost v buňkách; bez obrázku se nakreslí náhradní ikona). perk: observe|morale|supplies|intel|crossing|cover|hospital|tunnels; demolition = ženista +3 útok.

abilities.suppress: Suppression: hits two targets; the enemy loses 1 attack in the first round. May jam in the rain.
abilities.demolition: Demolition: +3 attack at the church, the brickworks and the quarry.
abilities.firstshot: First shot before the fight begins. Half attack in fog, +2 in clear weather.
abilities.heal: Patches up the worst wounded every round (+3) and saves one comrade from death.
abilities.initiative: Moves first. If the raid fails, gets everyone out: nobody is taken prisoner.
abilities.artillery: Calls one shell (5 damage) if the side holds the church or the outpost, or the sky is clear.
abilities.morale: Hot food: everyone else in the squad gets +1 attack and +1 defence.
abilities.faith: The squad never breaks and runs. Everyone starts with +2 health.
abilities.command: Orders: +1 attack for the whole squad in the first exchange. Goes for the weakest enemy.

@{handle} Noted, soldier. {loc}, tonight. Blacken your face. ({n}/{slots} {us})
full: @{handle} The {us} squad for {loc} is full ({slots}/{slots}). Next raid in a few days.

locations.name: Ruined Church of Saint-Ash
locations.desc: A shelled church with half a bell tower. The only high point in the valley.
locations.perkText: The tower sees for miles: signallers of the side that holds it can call down artillery on every raid.

locations.name: The Cemetery
locations.desc: Graves torn open by shells behind the church. Both sides bury their dead here at night.
locations.perkText: Morale: fewer losses on the line while under bombardment.

locations.name: Ruins of Verdel
locations.desc: What is left of the town of Verdel: cellars, chimneys and one stubborn bakery oven.
locations.perkText: Supplies from the cellars: fewer wounded on the line every day.

locations.name: Lonely Observation Post
locations.desc: A sandbagged hole far out in no man's land with a periscope and a field telephone.
locations.perkText: Intelligence: the side that holds it moves first on every raid, and its signallers can call artillery.

locations.name: Grey Mill
locations.desc: A stone mill by the canal. The only bridge left standing.
locations.perkText: The canal road: raiders arrive rested, +2 health for everyone on every raid.

locations.name: The Brickworks
locations.desc: Kilns and a tall chimney. Walls thick enough to stop a shell.
locations.perkText: Cover: the front line of the side that holds it is safer.

locations.name: Field Hospital at Calvary Farm
locations.desc: A farmhouse with red crosses painted on the roof. Not everyone respects them.
locations.perkText: The wounded of the side that holds it recover faster.

locations.name: The Bone Quarry
locations.desc: A chalk quarry full of old tunnels. Some say they run under both lines.
locations.perkText: Tunnels: sappers of the side that holds it get +2 attack on every raid.

tank._: 26. 11. (NÁVRH): rozkaz TANK z hlasování = jeden tank v nejhustším úseku vlastní první linie; v okruhu r px vlastní střelci střílí ×fire a nepřítel zasahuje vlastní vojáky ×exposed; jinde beze změny. Vypnout = smazat tento klíč (pak platí plošný fire 1,35 / exposed 1,1 z hlasování). Simulace: docs/MECHANICS.md

battle._note: Denní boj (engine/battle.js, docs/COMBAT_ROLES.md). Všechna čísla se dají ladit; dopad ukáže node tools/sim-battle.mjs --kpi (a --set klíč=hodnota). Pravděpodobnosti jsou na vojáka a den.
battle._balance: verze vyvážení: zvyš při každé změně čísel, zapisuje se do denních metrik (state.battle.stats)
battle._guns: Dělostřelectvo střílí až po první výhře v závodě o kótu (pak 3 dny bombardování). Do té doby se texty se slovy gunsWords nepoužijí a zásahy z pozadí jsou kulky, granáty, drát.
battle._hit: pozadí: dělostřelectvo, granáty, miny (~60 % zásahů). Pásmo 0.008–0.03
battle._severity: závažnost u pozadí: náhoda > light = lehce (60 %), > heavy = těžce (25 %), jinak kriticky (15 %)
battle._newbieDays: ochrana nováčků je VYPNUTÁ (0 dní, od 2026-11-12 na pokyn uživatele): kritický zásah i zhoršení rány hrozí od prvního dne. Dřív 3 dny bez kritického zásahu kulkou a bez zhoršení.

care._note: need = práce mediků na raněného za den (medik má roles.medic.work = 2). Na lůžku need 0 (léčí nemocnice). 19. 11. (uživatel): lehce 1 (dřív 0,4), těžce 2 (dřív 1), kriticky 3 (dřív 2), ať medici při velkých ztrátách nestíhají.

light._: lehce: leží v zákopu; s plnou péčí (1 medik) je druhý den v pořádku; bez péče se zahojí jen s baseHeal a hrozí zhoršení na těžce

heavy._: těžce: nosítka/lůžko; bez péče riziko zhoršení (v zákopu ×trench); hojí se od minDays s heal × péče (na lůžku × care místa)
heavy._resolve: 15. 11. (uživatel: rychleji ozdravovat nebo zabíjet): od minDays 1 se může zahojit; po maxDays 2 nocích se rozhodne: zahojí se s šancí resolveHeal + resolveCare × péče, jinak zemře.

crit._: kriticky: musí mít nosítka nebo lůžko, jinak noc nepřežije. Smrt za noc = dieBase × critRisk místa (nosítka 1) + dieNoCare × chybějící péče (na lůžku 0). Zlepší se na těžce po stabilize nocích na nosítkách s plnou péčí, po stabilizeBed na lůžku

linger._: 15. 11. (uživatel): těžce raněný bez lůžka může zemřít; riziko za noc = (base + perDay × dní od zranění) × (1 − care × péče mediků) × (v zákopu bez nosítek trench, a to už první noc), nejvýš max. Nováčci (newbieDays) chránění.

care._triage: triage: kritický bez místa vezme lůžko nebo nosítka těžce raněnému.
care._bed: lůžko = operace: první noc na lůžku kritický umírá s dieBase × critRisk místa, kdo přežije, je těžce raněný a druhý den se vrací na frontu (nejvýš 2 dny na lůžku); engine/battle.js

roles._covers: covers = kolik lidí poblíž jeden voják role pokryje (kulomet: nepřátelské střelce, spojař: vojáky, důstojník/spojka: střelce, kuchař: lehce raněné, kaplan: kriticky raněné na nosítkách). Účinek = plný účinek × min(1, počet role × covers / lidí poblíž): roste s poměrem, nikdy přes plný účinek.
roles._note: fire = šance za den, že voják v přední linii trefí nepřítele naproti (do roles.range px). severity = závažnost zásahu (jako u pozadí).

default._: podpůrné role (nosič, kuchař, kaplan, spojař, runner, ženista): občas vystřelí

rifleman._27: 27. 11. (uživatel: moc raněných, nosítka plná): puškař trefí méně (fire 0,25 → 0,18) a zásah je z 55 % lehký / 33 % těžký / 12 % kritický (dřív 40/40/20); smrtelnost těžkého zásahu 0,4 → 0,55, aby padlých nebylo míň.
rifleman._24: 24. 11. (uživatel): puškař má víc nábojů a střílí celý den: 3 výstřely denně, zásahy 40 % lehce / 40 % těžce / 20 % kriticky (dřív 1 výstřel, 70/18/12).

machinegunner._: potlačení: každý kulomet naproti sníží palbu nepřítele o suppress (nejvýš suppressMax)
machinegunner._24: 24. 11.: kulomet 2 výstřely denně (dál potlačuje palbu nepřátel poblíž, nejvýš o 30 %).

sniper._: pick = šance, že si vybere kulometčíka nebo důstojníka

officer._: velení: +lead palby a +xp zkušeností vojákům poblíž

runner._: spojka: rozkazy dojdou; bez důstojníka poblíž +relay palby vojákům poblíž

signaller._: telefon k dělostřelectvu: vojáci poblíž −counter zásahů z pozadí
signaller._24: 24. 11.: telefon k dělům proti střeleckým hnízdům: nepřátelští střelci poblíž spojařů trefí až o 25 % méně (podle pokrytí).

sapper._: oprava drátu v jeho úseku za den

cook._: lehce ranění poblíž: +heal šance zahojit se i bez mediků, zhoršení ×(1 − worsen)
cook._24: 24. 11.: lehce raněný u kuchaře potřebuje o polovinu méně práce mediků (relief), kuchař pomáhá hojit i ošetřované (always), pokryje 8 (dřív 4).

chaplain._: kaplan: smrt kritických na nosítkách ×(1 − faith × pokrytí); jeden kaplan pokryje covers umírajících
chaplain._24: 24. 11.: víra 0,35 (dřív 0,2), i u těžce raněných (méně umírají při dlouhém ležení a rozhodnutí po 2 nocích), pokryje 6 (dřív 3).

roles._shots19: 19. 11.: zpět na 1 výstřel denně, protože od teď střílí všichni vojáci ve všech liniích (dřív jen přední). 2 výstřely × všichni = ~110 padlých první den a do 3 dnů ~200 denně (medici by nestíhali); 1 výstřel = stabilně ~65 padlých a ~210 raněných denně při 1 400 hráčích.
roles._shots: 18. 11. (uživatel: na 500 hráčů je ~9 padlých denně málo, cíl ~30): každý střelec střílí 2× denně (2. kolo jen kdo zůstal zdravý, obě strany naráz), smrtelnost těžký 0,7 (dřív 0,25), kritický 0,8 (dřív 0,5), kritický od odstřelovače 0,9 (dřív 0,6). Simulace: ~32 padlých a ~90 raněných denně za obě strany.
roles._killHeavy: 15. 11. (uživatel: musí se umírat i přímo palbou): kritický zásah kulkou zabije na místě s kill 0,5 (dřív 0,2), těžký s killHeavy 0,12.
roles._saturation: VYPNUTO 15. 11. (uživatel: víc střelců = větší palebná síla). Dřív: střelec trefoval méně, když bylo u něj víc vlastních střelců než nepřátel na dostřel.
roles._kill: kill: šance, že kritický zásah kulkou zabije na místě (roles.<role>.kill přebíjí). Ostatní smrti vznikají z nedostatku lůžek, nosítek a mediků.
roles._killHeavy24: 24. 11. (návrh G3): těžký zásah zabije na místě 0,4 (dřív 0,7): víc raněných doleží na nosítka, rozhodují medici.

xp._: mult násobí hlavní schopnost role: palbu, práci medika, opravy ženisty

maxDeaths._: jen pojistka proti chybě v kódu (25 % strany za den); běžné ztráty dávají statistiky (13. 11. na pokyn uživatele, dřív 5 % a blokovalo to umírání)

wire._cover: 15. 11.: celý drát sníží zásahy o 40 % (dřív 15 %), roztrhaný drát je znát.

letter._: dopis z domova (hráč ho na webu pošle svému vojákovi, přihlášený majitel, jednou za den): voják má v příštím tahu o `cut` menší šanci na zásah všeho druhu; neodeslaný dopis = žádný buff (retence)

battle._shootLines: 19. 11. (uživatel: linie nerozlišovat): všichni vojáci na frontě střílí a jdou zasáhnout stejně, ať stojí v kterékoli linii. Dřív jen přední a vojáci v podpůrné a spojovací linii navíc nemohli být zasaženi (chyběli v battle.line), takže noví hráči řazení dozadu nebojovali vůbec.

pillbox._: 19. 11. (uživatel): bunkry zůstávají natrvalo a válka je opotřebovává (denně 6 %, pod bombardováním +10 %, každý zásah raidera do zákopu +0,4 %), každý zdravý ženista strany opraví 0,4 % (nejvýš 15 % denně). Stav = 1 − ruined, bonus palby a ruiny na mapě podle něj.

raid._: 18. 11. (uživatel): noční raid; přihláška RAID pod postem s `raid: true`, vyhodnocení v příštích novinách (engine/battle.js krok 0b, engine/nightraid.js). base = šance vpadnout a zasáhnout obránce, +perGap × potrhaný drát nepřítele, −perMG za každý kulomet obránců poblíž; weather násobí (mlha a déšť pomáhají). Zásah zblízka: hlavně těžký a kritický, kill/killHeavy = smrt obránce (počítá se do závodu o zabití). Cesta zpět: hurt + hurtPerMG × kulomety.
raid._deadly: 19. 11. (uživatel: raid má být opravdu smrtící): až 2 souboje za noc (druhý jen po vítězném prvním), smrtelnost zblízka kritický 0,95, těžký 0,75; raideři ráno v bitvě nestřílí (vyčerpaní).
raid._24: 24. 11. (uživatel: raid má být velmi nebezpečný, výhoda puškaři): riziko na cestě zpět 0,4 (dřív 0,25), smrt kritického 0,75 / těžkého 0,5; puškař vyhrává souboj ×1,3 a má riziko ×0,6.

wiring.returned: At dusk {name} walked back into {sector}, covered in mud, and asked for a place on the wiring party. The sergeant crossed the name off the missing list.
wiring._: wiring party: dobrovolníci (komentář WIRE pod postem s wiring: true) v noci opraví drát; riziko = (base + perFire × palba hlídek nepřítele na dostřel, kdo jde ven, nehlídá) × počasí × bombardování × ženista; zásah = běžné zranění (péče jako jinde)

news.side: {side} wire in no man's land is down to {pct}% after {cause}. In {gaps} of {secs} sectors there are gaps a man could walk through.
why: Wire is what stops a raid before it reaches the trench, and it soaks up the bullets that cross the line. Without it, every post on the fire step is easier to hit.
Barbed wire is the first line of defense. It slows a raid, holds up a patrol and gives the men behind it cover. A trench with broken wire is a trench with an open door.
Every yard of wire is a yard the enemy has to cut through before reaching the fire step. Where the wire is gone, the men on watch are easier to hit.
Wire does not stop a bullet by itself, but it keeps the enemy at a distance and gives the men on the fire step cover. Thin wire means more men hit.
call: So the wiring parties go out after dark. They crawl out with coils of barbed wire and corkscrew posts that twist into the mud without a sound, and when a flare goes up they drop flat and wait for the dark. Volunteers: comment WIRE under the wiring order on Instagram.

Wiring parties fix it at night. They crawl out with coils of wire and corkscrew posts, work in the dark and lie flat when a flare goes up. Volunteers: comment WIRE under the wiring order on Instagram.
Only volunteers can mend it. After dark they crawl out with pliers, gloves and coils of wire, and come back before dawn. To volunteer, comment WIRE under the wiring order on Instagram.
The front needs hands on the wire tonight. It is slow, quiet, dangerous work, and every yard counts. Comment WIRE under the wiring order on Instagram to join a wiring party.
news._: zpráva v Gazette, když má strana průměrný drát pod 'below' (nebo je pod bombardováním a drát má pod 'below'); engine/battle.js h, why a call můžou být pole variant (každý den jiná).
news.mendedShelled: In the night {n} volunteers crawled out and put up {yards} yards of new wire. Then the last shells came down and tore much of it apart again. Without the wiring parties it would be down to {without}%.

wiring._roles: 24. 11. (uživatel): na drátu má výhodu ženista: poloviční riziko, oprava ×1,5.

mine._: mina: hit = šance zásahu každého v zasaženém úseku/okně; kill = smrt na místě u kritického zásahu (jen mina z kóty); men/tries = okno nejhustší první linie; counter* = šance, že nepřátelští ženisti tunel zavalí (5 % + 0,1 % za ženistu, max 25 %)

shell._kill: kill: šance, že kritický zásah granátem zabije na místě (lůžko ani medik nepomůže).
shell._careCut: careCut: raněný, který ještě leží v ostřelovaném zákopu (ne na nosítkách ani lůžku), dostane jen 1 − careCut péče mediků (0,6 → 40 %); 13. 11. na pokyn uživatele

aidPost.name: Aid post
aidPost._: obvaziště (vždy): care = hojení těžkého na lůžku ×care proti nosítkům s plnou péčí; critRisk = riziko smrti kritického za noc ×critRisk proti nosítkům
aidPost._stretchersPerMedic: stretchersPerMedic: každý medik schopný služby nese nosítka navíc.

dugout.name: Hospital dugout
dugout.done: dug a deep hospital dugout behind the reserve line, out of rifle range: 4 beds

hospital.name: Field hospital
hospital.done: built a large field hospital behind the reserve line, out of rifle range: 30 beds, an operating table and a surgeon's lamp
hospital.start: raised a large field hospital behind the reserve line, out of rifle range: 30 beds, an operating table and a surgeon's lamp. The first patients go in tomorrow
hospital._: 26. 11.: výsledek hlasování HOSPITAL (build dugout) staví tohle; velkou stavbou s 30 lůžky NAVÍC k obvazišti a zemnicím (lůžka a nosítka se sčítají)

sandbags.name: Sandbag parapets
sandbags.done: raised the parapets with fresh sandbags: fewer men hit

wire.name: New wire belts
wire.done: ran new belts of wire across no-man's land

battle._daily: Denní meze raněných (min 1 / max 30 na 80 vojáků) odstraněny 14. 11. na pokyn uživatele: ztráty dává jen náhoda (v simulaci se meze stejně neuplatnily). Engine je umí, kdyby byly potřeba: battle.daily { min, max, shellMax, per }.
battle._hitLying: 15. 11. (uživatel): na raněné, kteří od včerejška leží v zákopu bez nosítek, se střílí taky; lehký se zhorší, těžký a kritický zemře.

news.text: From the gun pit behind the {us} line, {gun} shelled {them} sectors {from} to {to}. {hit} men were hit, {killed} killed outright. The gun is at {cond}%.
news.rebuilt: After days of work the sappers have it firing again.
news.destroyed: {them} fire finally found the gun pit behind the {us} line. {gun} lies on its side in the mud. Only sappers with time to spare can bring it back.
news.wreck: {us} sappers worked on the wreck of {gun} all day. It stands at {cond}%. At 50% it fires again.

gun._: 20. 11. (uživatel): těžké dělo (odměna kóty reward 'gun', engine/gun.js). Každý den okno `men` vojáků nepřítele po sobě podle x (nejhustší z `tries` náhodných), zásah hit × síla podle stavu (power), kritický zabije s kill. Stav: −wear za den palby, −min(fireMax, perShooter × zdraví odstřelovači+kulometčíci nepřítele), protipalba nepřátelského děla counterChance × counter × jeho síla. Oprava jen z volné práce ženistů (po drátu ve vlastním úseku): sapperRepair za jednotku práce, nejvýš maxRepair denně. 0 = zničené, střílí znovu od rebuild.

house._note: Odznaky rodu (engine/house.js): udělí se jednou a zůstávají v rodu napříč generacemi. Rodinné album na webu ukazuje i medaile a tituly všech generací.

_storyShare: Podíl vojáků, kteří dostanou každý den zápis do deníku (1 = každý, jeden zápis za den; dřív 0,25). Při velkém počtu hráčů roste stav (data/state.json) o ~220 B na vojáka a den.

cards._note: Sběratelské kartičky (docs/CARDS.md, nasazeno 24. 11.): kdo se vrátí živý z wiring party, nočního raidu nebo letu, najde se šancí chance kartičku. Bez stropu, pilot nejvýš 1. Kartičky patří rodu (dědí se). Obrázky web/public/assets/cards/card_<id>.png (54×87) a back.png.

entry.wire: Out on the wire, {name}'s hand closed on something flat in the mud: a sweetheart card, '{card}' ({rarity}). {name} dried it inside a helmet and kept it.
entry.raid: Back from the raid, {name} found a sweetheart card in a coat pocket that was not there before: '{card}' ({rarity}). Nobody asked where it came from.
entry.pilot: After the flight, {name} found a sweetheart card tucked behind the compass: '{card}' ({rarity}). The mechanic swore he never saw it.
entry.letter: Inside the letter for {name} there was something extra, slipped between the pages: a sweetheart card, '{card}' ({rarity}). {name} looked at it for a long time.

news.one: One sweetheart card was picked up in the mud.
news.many: {n} sweetheart cards were picked up in the mud.

cards.lore: Sweetheart cards were printed in the capital and sold for a penny. Men kept them in their helmets. They turn up in the mud after wiring parties, raids and flights. Nobody throws one away: when a man falls, his cards stay with his family.
cards._letter: 24. 11. (uživatel: miniaturní šance na kartičku v dopise): 0,5 % na dopis, z dopisu nejvýš 1 kartička na vojáka (cap.letter).

_inheritMedals: 20. 11. (uživatel): na živého nástupce přechází podpora (War Bonds, hvězda) i odznaky narukování (First Wave, First Thousand); vlastní zásluhy (medaile kót, Raider's Cross…) zůstávají padlému, v albu rodu jsou vidět všechny.

support._note: Dobrovolná podpora přes Patreon (Ko-fi zamítlo platby 14. 11.): medaile bez herní výhody. url = stránka Patreonu (prázdné = tlačítko na webu se neukáže), platform = název služby v textech webu.
support.name: War Bonds
support.line: supported the making of Mud & Iron
support.entry: {name} bought War Bonds for the front. The quartermaster pinned the ribbon on personally: 'The front remembers who kept it fed.'
support.newsHead: The front stands in their debt
support.newsText: {names} bought War Bonds and put their own money behind the line. Every man in the trenches owes them. The guns stay fed and the front will not forget it.

support._medals: 24. 11. (uživatel): pixelové medaile podporovatelů na kartě vojáka a v rodu (web/src/keepsakes.js), jen nejvyšší úroveň. Officers' Mess = medaile officers-star, Field Post = war-bonds + pes, War Bonds = war-bonds. Obrázky web/public/assets/medals/.png (varianta A z docs/mockups/medals/support).
support._buttons: buttons: false = tlačítka Support na webu skrytá (13.–14. 11. byla skrytá, Ko-fi zamítlo platby); od 14. 11. zapnuto s odkazem na Patreon.

_officerBalance: Vyrovnání poručíků (2026-11-12): nováček bez přání role ze strany s méně poručíky je poručík, strana s víc poručíky žádného nedostane, při rovnosti běžné losování. false = jen losování.

shells._: Souboj komentářů (engine/shells.js, 16. 11.): pod postem s `shells` je každý komentář granát pro stranu komentujícího (strop cap na účet); ranní noviny: vítěz rozbije podíl base + (1 − base) × (víc − míň) / víc bunkrů (rozkaz target) poraženého.

pilot._note: Role PILOT (docs/MECHANICS.md 2026-11-17): rifleman = bonus palby puškařů strany, shotDown = denní šance sestřelení, perTenMG = +šance za každých 10 nepřátelských kulometčíků, deathShare = podíl smrti při sestřelení, grounded = počasí bez letu

dog._: Trench Dog (21. 11.): pes pro Field Post a Officers' Mess; jméno i plemeno losuje hra (200 jmen, uživatel: žádné ruční vybírání); psí příběh v deníku jen občas (12 % dní ≈ jednou za týden); příkazy dog/undog/renameDog; engine/dog.js

winter._: 22. 11. 2026 (uživatel): týden 1 sněží + poprašek, týden 2 víc sněhu, týden 3 plná zima; points = [den od start, pokrytí 0..1], mezi body plynule (web/src/winter.js)

letters._: 24. 11.: věty o dopisu z domova (engine/roster.js, pošta); střídají se po dnech, ať denní odesílatel nemá pořád stejný zápis.
lines: A letter from home reached {n} before dusk. {n} read it twice and slept a little easier.
Mail came up the line with a letter for {n}. {n} read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
A letter from home found {n} before the night shift. {n} folded it small and kept it close.
The mail bag came up with the soup. There was a letter for {n}, and the soup went cold while {n} read it.
{n} got a letter today. The handwriting was shaky, but the news was good. The letter went inside the helmet, for luck.
A letter for {n} came with a pressed flower inside. {n} showed the flower to nobody.
{n} read the new letter by the light of a match, then another match, then a third.
The corporal called out the mail. {n} heard the name and almost ran.
The letter for {n} was mostly about the weather at home. {n} read that part twice too.
A letter reached {n} in the rain. The ink ran a little, but every word that mattered was still there.
{n} kept the new letter in a breast pocket all day, and touched the pocket now and then to check it was there.
There was a letter for {n}. Someone at home had drawn a small picture in the corner. {n} laughed for the first time in days.
A letter came for {n} with a sketch of the kitchen at home. {n} pinned it to the dugout wall.
The letter for {n} smelled faintly of soap. {n} held it close for a long time before opening it.
Someone at home had written the address three times, to be sure. The letter reached {n} anyway.
{n} got a letter full of small news: a new calf, a broken gate, a wedding in the spring.
The letter for {n} had a few coins taped inside. They would buy almost nothing here, but {n} kept them.
A thin letter reached {n}. Only five lines long, and {n} knew every one of them by heart before supper.
{n} read the letter out loud to the squad, skipping the private parts. The men asked to hear it again.
A letter for {n} came with a photograph. {n} looked at it for a long time and said nothing.
The letter for {n} ended with 'come home soon'. {n} read the last line more than the rest.
A letter reached {n} with a child's drawing of a soldier. The soldier in the drawing was smiling. {n} tried to as well.
The censor had blacked out two words in the letter for {n}. {n} guessed what they were and laughed.
{n} found a letter on the fire step, left by the runner. {n} read it while the kettle boiled.
A letter for {n} came all the way from home in nine days. {n} counted them on the envelope.
There was a letter for {n} and a little tobacco folded inside. The tobacco went round the squad. The letter did not.
The letter for {n} asked if the food was good. {n} wrote back that it was. That was a lie, but a kind one.
{n} got a letter with a recipe in it. Nobody in the trench had any of the things it needed.
A letter came for {n} with a ribbon tied around it. {n} kept the ribbon in a tunic pocket.
The letter for {n} had been in the rain somewhere along the way. {n} dried it by the stove, page by page.
{n} read the letter, folded it, unfolded it, and read it again. The sentry pretended not to see.
A letter for {n} said the whole street was asking about the front. {n} did not know where to begin the answer.
The letter for {n} was written in pencil, with a lot of crossing out. {n} liked the crossed-out parts best.
The runner said a letter for {n} had come up with the ammunition. {n} went to get it before the ammunition.
{n} got a letter with a pressed leaf from the tree by the front door at home.
A short letter reached {n}: everyone is well, the dog misses you. {n} read the part about the dog twice.
{n} got a letter from a sister, written in pencil on the back of a flour bag. {n} read it standing up, and then sitting down.
The mail sergeant held up an envelope and shouted a name. It was {n}. The whole trench clapped.
A letter came for {n} from a little town {he} had not seen in a year. Inside was a newspaper clipping about the harvest.
{n} read the letter from {his} father twice. It was short. It said: we are proud of you, and the dog misses you.
There was a parcel for {n}: socks, a cake, and a note that said eat the cake first. {n} ate the cake first.
{n} got a letter from a friend still at home. It was mostly about a girl and a horse, and {n} could not tell which one mattered.
A thick letter reached {n} in the trench. Six pages, all about the new baby. {n} read it aloud to anyone who stood still.
{n} unfolded the letter carefully. A dried leaf fell out, and {n} put it in a pocket without a word.
Mail call. {n} got three letters at once and sat down on an ammunition box to put them in order.
The letter for {n} was addressed to the wrong trench and had been to two others first. It was slightly muddy and entirely welcome.
{n} got a postcard of the old church at home. The tower was drawn in with ink in case {n} had forgotten it.
A letter came for {n} from the man who owns the shop back home. It said {n}'s job would be waiting. {n} read that line to the squad.
{n} could not read the letter in the dark, so {he} held it close to a candle and read it one line at a time.
The letter for {n} had only one line: 'Come home soon.' {n} read it more times than a one-line letter should be read.
{n} got a letter from an old teacher, with a note about spelling. {n} laughed, and fixed two words in the reply.
A letter for {n} came with a photograph of a very large cat. The squad passed it around and agreed that it looked well fed.
{n} read a letter from {his} brother. It said everything was fine. {n} read between the lines and wrote back at once.
A small envelope reached {n} with a lock of hair inside. {n} put it inside the helmet lining and said nothing for an hour.
{n} got a letter in a child's handwriting. Every sentence started with 'Please' and ended with 'Come back.' {n} had to go and stand outside for a minute.
The mail wagon was late, but there was a letter for {n}. {n} read it with a cold biscuit in one hand.
{n} got a letter from home with a recipe in it. {He} read it out to the cook, who said it could not be done with army flour.
A letter from a cousin found {n} at the supply dump. The news was bad, but {n} was glad of the news.
{n} got a letter and a pair of mittens. The mittens were too big. {n} wore them anyway.
There was a letter for {n} that smelled of pipe smoke. {n} knew at once who had written it, and smiled for the first time all week.
{n} wrote back at once, by the light of the stove. It took an hour and came to four lines.
A letter from a neighbor reached {n}. It told {n} that the fence was fixed, the cow was fine, and the roof still leaked.
{n} read the letter from the girl next door twice and then put it away, to keep it for later.
{n} carried the letter around all day without opening it, because {he} wanted to save it for after dark.
A letter came for {n}, and the whole squad fell silent while it was read. It was good news. The cheering lasted an hour.
{n} got a bundle of old newspapers from home. {He} read them in order, even the parts about the weather.
The letter for {n} was in a stranger's handwriting. It was from a woman who had met {n}'s mother at church. It said: she is well, and she prays for you.
{n} held the letter up to the light to make sure there was nothing hidden in it. There was only a note that said: write soon.
A small parcel arrived for {n}: a pencil and a pad of paper. The note said: write to us. {n} began at once.
{n} got a letter in a language only {he} and {his} family speak. Nobody else in the squad could read a word, and {n} liked it that way.
Another letter for {n} today. The sergeant said {n} was the most popular man in the company. {n} said it was only because of the stamps.
{n} got a letter from the old neighbor, who wrote that {n}'s dog now sleeps at the front door every night.
A letter came for {n}, folded in a tiny square. It took a minute to unfold it, and a minute longer to believe it.
{n} read the letter in the latrine because it was the only quiet place in the trench. No one was surprised.
The corporal handed {n} a letter and said it had come all the way from the capital. {n} said it had come further than that.
{n} got a letter that began with the words: 'Don't worry.' It took {n} three readings to stop worrying.
{n} got a letter from home and a tin of tea. The tea was shared. The letter was not.
A friendly letter reached {n} from a nurse who had once treated {his} father. {n} did not know what to make of it, and kept it.
{n} was handed a letter at dawn watch. {He} did not open it until the sun was fully up.
The mail bag had a letter for {n} and nothing for anyone else. {n} read it as quietly as {he} could.
{n} spent the evening answering a letter. The first draft was too long. The second was too short. The third was just right.
